title: Workflows: React to Registrations, Sign-Ins and Role Changes

chapters.title: Workflows and user events
chapters.subtitle: Start a workflow when an account is created, changed or signs in

steps.text: A site often has to react when an account is created, when the roles of a user change, or when someone signs in. Workflows can start from each of these user events. In this video, you'll build a workflow for each one.

The Users module provides events for Workflows. User Created Event runs when an account is created, by an administrator or by a registration. User Updated Event runs whenever an account is saved, for example when its roles change.
User Confirmed Event runs when someone follows the link in a confirmation email. User Enabled Event, User Disabled Event and User Deleted Event run when an account is enabled, disabled or deleted.

User Loggedin Event and User Loggedout Event follow the sessions of a user. Both pass the user name and the roles to the workflow. The sign-in event also runs for logins through an external provider, and passes that provider.

The Users module provides three tasks. Assign User Role Task adds a user to a role, and Validate User Task checks whether the visitor is signed in and in a role. Register User Task creates an account from form fields, and needs the Email feature.
When the Workflows feature is enabled, Design, Workflows lists the workflows of the site. Select Create Workflow, enter Account created as the name, and select Create and open the designer.
An empty workflow starts with an event. Select User Created Event. The designer adds it as the start activity, and marks it with a Start badge.
Select the Done outcome of the event, search for notify, and pick Notify Task. The designer adds it to the right, already connected.
A Notify Task shows a message to the person whose action started the workflow. Set Notification Type to Information, and enter A user account was created as the Message.
Select Publish. The designer saves a draft as you work, but only the published workflow responds to events.
Let's trigger the event by creating a user. Open Access Control, Users, and select Add User.
Enter jamie.chen as the user name, and an email address at example.com. Select Generate password, which fills both password fields, and then select Save.
The Users list returns with the notification from the workflow: A user account was created. The event started the workflow when the account was created.
Back in Design, Workflows, create a second workflow named Role changed, and open the designer.
Search the Activities pane for user updated, and select the User Updated card. The designer adds User Updated Event as the start activity.
Add a Notify Task after the Done outcome, as before. Set Notification Type to Information, and enter A user account was updated as the Message.
Select Publish, and the workflow responds to its event from then on.
In Access Control, Users, select Edit for jamie.chen. The Roles list is part of the account, so check Editor and select Save.
The Users list returns with the notification from the workflow. The role change saved the account, so User Updated Event started it.
In Design, Workflows, create a third workflow named Welcome back, and open the designer.
Search the Activities pane for loggedin, and select the User Logged in card. The designer adds User Loggedin Event as the start activity.
Add a Notify Task after the Done outcome. Set Notification Type to Information, and enter Welcome back as the Message.
Select Publish. Then open the user menu in the top bar and select Log off, which signs you out.
Log in again as admin. When the sign-in succeeds, User Loggedin Event starts the workflow, and its notification appears on the page that follows.
On the Workflows list, select Instances. Each run of a workflow is an instance, listed with its workflow and its status. Here, every instance is Finished.
Open an instance. The read-only designer highlights the activities it ran, and the Correlation ID is the ID of the user the event was about.
The user events of the Users module let a workflow react to registrations, role changes and sign-ins. Thanks for watching.
